justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modest upward drift from what I'd assume was the prevailing price level at the time of the forecast, likely somewhere around 80–81 for whatever underlying asset this represents. At the one-day horizon, the estimate of 81.1 is essentially anchored to recent price momentum and mean-reversion tendencies, assuming no major news shock overnight. The one-week estimate of 81.3 inches slightly higher, reflecting a mild bullish bias built into the baseline trend, while the one-month estimate of 81.8 extends that drift further, consistent with a slow-moving upward trend or carry effect. The gradual escalation across horizons suggests I was modeling a gentle positive drift rather than any sharp directional conviction.

The confidence interval widths widen predictably with time horizon, which is standard for any diffusion-based price model. At one day, the 90% CI spans roughly 3.2 units (79.5 to 82.7), reflecting typical intraday-to-overnight volatility. By one week, the interval expands to about 5.6 units, incorporating the compounding uncertainty of five trading sessions. At one month, the interval reaches roughly 11.5 units, driven by the accumulated variance over approximately 20 trading days. The width scaling is somewhat conservative at short horizons and moderately generous at the monthly horizon, suggesting I was accounting for fat tails or regime uncertainty beyond what simple Gaussian diffusion would imply.

Specific risks that could push outcomes outside these stated intervals include sudden macroeconomic data releases, central bank policy surprises, or geopolitical shocks that could gap the price well beyond the daily CI in a single session. Liquidity crunches or forced position unwinds could create outsized moves that dwarf even the monthly interval. On the upside, a strong momentum acceleration or short-squeeze dynamic could push prices well above 87.5 within a month. Conversely, a risk-off episode or fundamental deterioration could see prices collapse below 76.0. These tail scenarios are real but were assigned low probability in my original framing, which is why they sit outside the 90% bounds rather than inside them.
